column1: # The CI dependency graph (#1411). This file is the source; the workflow is checked
# against it, not the other way round.
#   stage <TAB> needs (comma-separated, `-` for none) <TAB> why the edge exists
#   1. `lint` is a leaf for every *stage*. No stage may list it in `needs`. A lint finding is
#      a verdict on the tree, not on whether anything compiles: `build: needs: [workspace,
#      lint]` once skipped the build, and every stage downstream of it, so seven subjects
#      never ran and the gate accused five of them of failing (#1411).
#      `ci-report` and `gate` are the exception because they are not stages: their subject
#      IS every stage's result, so they must name every stage, `lint` included. The set is
#      fixed in the checker; a third aggregator is an error, not a convention.
#   2. An edge exists only when the upstream's result decides the downstream's subject. A
#      workspace that does not compile makes a test run meaningless; a lint finding does not.
# `portable`, `shell` and `wasm-gates` hang off nothing, because each has its own subject and
# none consumes a build artifact (#1410 is the same rule applied to one stage).
